contracts.action: Checkpoint capture resolves common dir, user index path and HEAD existence with one combined `git rev-parse` instead of up to three separate processes
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous path: resolveGitCommonDir (apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:819), hasHeadCommit (:793), and an inline `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index` inside the reuse-index block
contracts.before_after: Before: three separate rev-parse calls (common dir, HEAD check, index path). After: one call; the output is accepted only when the exit code is 0 or 1 and the line count is exactly 4 or 3 with a trailing empty line. Anything else (git < 2.31 echoing --path-format, a newline in the path, exit 128 outside a repo) falls back to the old separate commands, so error operation labels and exit codes are the same as before.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. Checkpoint capture starts fewer git processes.
contracts.failure_mode: Not in a repo: exit 128 gives headChecked=false, so the fallback resolveGitCommonDir fails with the old operation label and exit 128 (asserted at GitVcsDriver.test.ts:998-1000). The combined call uses allowNonZeroExit, so the darwin fsync-retry branch (VcsProcess.ts:279-298) does not apply, but that branch only matters for commands carrying fsync args. A newline in the path inflates the line count and always forces the fallback. Fallback paths run only the commands the old code ran.

summary: I found no defects in either file. The combined `rev-parse` call has strict output validation (exit code 0 or 1, exact line count with a trailing empty line). When validation fails, it falls back to the old separate commands. The fallback covers git older than 2.31, which echoes `--path-format`, and paths containing a newline. Running outside a repo still fails with the old operation label and exit 128. The new call uses the capture operation, which only affects the retry logic in `VcsProcess.run`. That logic is bypassed for commands with `allowNonZeroExit` or `onStdoutChunk`, so the new call is unaffected. The new tests cover the committed and unborn HEAD cases, the outside-a-repo failure, and the newline-path fallback. The PR title says 8 git processes instead of 10. By my count of the commands the test asserts, it is 9 instead of 11 with a commit and 7 instead of 8 on an unborn HEAD. I did not report this as a finding.
